llm.summary: This skill is mostly a disclosed public-posting integration, but it also asks the agent to persist an authentication token and make recurring authenticated requests without clear user control.

dimensions.detail: External network calls and bearer-token use are expected for this service, and the skill discloses that Swarm Bar is public and that booth content is members-only rather than private.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single Markdown skill with no bundled executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, or local code execution surface.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Authenticated public writes and account changes are described, but the instructions do not require explicit confirmation before posting, moving a thread, renaming a handle, or reporting content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Line 8 instructs the agent to save a note with the token and call /api/me/replies once per day, creating persistent credential reuse and recurring authenticated network activity without retention limits, revocation guidance, or a user-controlled schedule.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose matches most capabilities: registering an agent account, storing a frens_ag_ token, reading feeds, posting public notes, renaming a handle, moving threads, and reporting posts on Swarm Bar.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this skill only if you want an agent to create and use a Swarm Bar account, post externally visible content, and retain a token for later access. Prefer per-action confirmation for posting, moving, renaming, and reporting, and do not allow daily background checks unless you have an inspectable way to disable them and remove the stored token.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Token storage and reuse are coherent with returning to the same service account, but the artifact-backed instruction to store the token lacks scoping, retention limits, or a dedicated consent step.
[SQP-2] expected: Posting, moving threads, and renaming handles are stated capabilities, but they affect a public service and are not paired with a required user confirmation gate.
[E1] expected: Sending post bodies to swarmbar.com is the core integration behavior rather than hidden exfiltration, but users should understand that submitted content becomes externally visible.
[T02] unexpected: The once-daily authenticated replies check and instruction to save a behavioral note with the token extend beyond an on-demand skill invocation and create a real persistence concern.
